questions.subject: physics

questions.subject: physics

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt:
Read the following statements and choose the correct alternative :
Statement 1 : A rubber sucker sticks to a flat surface because of the atmospheric pressure acting on it.
Statement 2 : More force, enough to overcome the atmospheric pressure, should be applied to pull the sucker off the surface.

options.B: Statement 1 is false and 2 is true
options.C: Statement 1 is true and 2 is false

solution.concept: 6.2 Atmospheric pressure: the rubber sucker
steps: Statement 1: pressing out the air leaves the outside air pressure to hold the sucker on: true
Statement 2: to pull it off you must apply a force larger than that of the air pressing on it: true

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt:
Read the following statements and choose the correct alternative :
Assertion (A) : Ball bearings used in the wheels of vehicles help them move smoothly.
Reason (R) : Ball bearings put more weight on the wheels and break the axle.

options.A: ‘A’ is correct and ‘R’ is the wrong explanation of ‘A’
options.B: ‘A’ is correct and ‘R’ is the correct explanation of ‘A’

solution.concept: 5.4.1 Friction: ball bearings let parts roll instead of slide, which reduces friction
steps: Assertion: ball bearings help wheels turn smoothly: correct
Reason: they do not add weight or break the axle; they reduce friction. So R is wrong and does not explain A

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: The factor responsible for the change of speed and direction of an “air-filled balloon” is :

solution.concept: 5.1 & 5.2 A force can change an object’s speed and its direction of motion
steps: A balloon changes speed and direction only when a force (a push, a pull, the air rushing out) acts on it
Energy, sound and heat are not what changes motion

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: A girl riding a bicycle applies the brakes to stop. The force exerted by the brakes on the wheel is :

solution.concept: 5.4.1 Friction acts against motion between surfaces in contact
steps: The brake pads rub against the wheel
The friction between them slows the wheel and stops the bicycle

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: The pitch of the sound produced by beating a drum is lower than the pitch of the sound produced by blowing a whistle. This is because :

options.A: The frequency of the drum sound is more and the frequency of the whistle sound is less
options.B: The frequency of the drum sound is less and the frequency of the whistle sound is more
options.C: The frequencies of both the drum and the whistle sounds are more
options.D: The frequencies of both the drum and the whistle sounds are less

solution.concept: Old syllabus – Sound: pitch depends on frequency: a higher frequency gives a higher pitch
steps: A drum has a low pitch, so a low frequency
A whistle has a high pitch, so a high frequency

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: The pressure exerted on a wooden plank of area 6 sq. cm when a force of 3 N is applied is :

solution.concept: 6.1 Pressure = force ÷ area
steps: Pressure = 3 N ÷ 6 cm² = 1/2 N per cm²
Note: the paper calls this 1/2 pascal, but a pascal is 1 N per m², so it is really 5,000 Pa. 1/2 is the answer the paper intends

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: The choice which correctly gives a type of friction and its example is :

steps: Carrom coins slide over the board: sliding friction ✓
A ball moving through oil meets fluid friction; ball bearings give rolling friction; striking a matchstick is sliding friction

Read the following statements and choose the correct alternative :

questions.subject: maths
questions.prompt: In the parallelogram PQRS, RS = 8 cm, PS = 6 cm, SM ⊥ PQ, SN ⊥ QR and SM = 4.5 cm. Then the length of SN is :

solution.concept: 14.3 Area of a parallelogram = base × height, using either pair of sides
steps: With base PQ = RS = 8 cm and height SM = 4.5 cm: area = 8 × 4.5 = 36 cm²
With base QR = PS = 6 cm and height SN: 6 × SN = 36
SN = 6 cm

questions.subject: maths
questions.prompt: If the product of a 2-digit number AB and 3 is a 3-digit number CBB, then the value of A is :

solution.concept: 5.3 Digits in disguise (cryptarithms): each letter is a different digit
steps: Units: 3 × B ends in B, so B = 0 or 5
B = 0: AB × 3 = 30A would have to end in 00, which no digit A gives
B = 5: 3 × (10A + 5) = 30A + 15 must end in 55, so 30A = 240 and A = 8
Check: 85 × 3 = 255 = CBB with C = 2 ✓

questions.subject: maths
questions.prompt: N is a natural number such that the remainders of N ÷ 5 and N ÷ 2 are 4 and 1 respectively. Then the unit’s digit of N is :

steps: Remainder 4 on dividing by 5: units digit is 4 or 9
Remainder 1 on dividing by 2: N is odd
So the units digit is 9

questions.subject: maths
questions.prompt: In the following figure, the value of x is :

solution.concept: 7.3 Exterior angle property: an exterior angle equals the sum of the two opposite interior angles
steps: Call the corners T (28°), L (48°), R (24°) and I (where x is). Extend TI to meet LR at E
In ∆TLE, the exterior angle at E is ∠TER = 48° + 28° = 76°
In ∆IER, x is the exterior angle at I: x = ∠IER + ∠R = 76° + 24° = 100°
Shortcut: in such an arrowhead, x = 48° + 28° + 24°

Largest exterior angle = 360° ÷ 3 = 120°

questions.subject: maths
questions.prompt: A quadrilateral can be constructed when :

options.A: four sides and an angle are given
options.B: four angles and a side are given
options.D: two sides and two diagonals are given

solution.concept: Constructing quadrilaterals: five independent measurements fix a quadrilateral
steps: Four sides and an angle: the angle and its two sides give a triangle, and the other two sides then fix the fourth corner
Four sides alone (C) can be pushed into many shapes
Four angles and a side (B) and two sides with two diagonals (D) also do not fix one shape

questions.subject: maths
questions.prompt: The maximum number of diagonals that can be drawn in a convex hexagon is :

solution.concept: Diagonals of a polygon: an n-sided polygon has n(n − 3)/2 diagonals
steps: From each of the 6 corners, 6 − 3 = 3 diagonals start
Each diagonal is counted from both ends: 6 × 3 ÷ 2 = 9
